findings.reason: a control that a correct held/queued dispatch also satisfies cannot distinguish the defect; the gate needs a control that fails only on a shut-gate refusal, and the second case needs its own.
findings.text: The node's one negative control ("at the base revision the refused dispatch leaves at least one pointer") cannot show the guard fires, because a `LaneHeld` router hold legitimately leaves a queued pointer at the base revision too (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:4725-4761`), so the control passes whether or not the refusal wrote anything. The second case ("within the bound it is retired, naming why") carries no control of its own, and its bound is named only by reference (the 900s stranded-launch bound), not stated in the section.

findings.reason: if the four pointers are §49's duplicates, s50 repairs a mechanism that may already hold at base and re-does work §49 owns; the node needs a single-dispatch reproduction of a refused dispatch leaving a pointer before it repairs anything.
findings.text: The Why reads the four pointers for head 391070b46221 as the refused dispatch's own output, but the plan's own §49 (whose Why measured seven (node, head) pairs getting two or three reviews within fourteen seconds, from "the session follower's reflex, the station sweep and a coordinator's direct dispatch") documents exactly this signature: several dispatchers reaching one delivered run at once. A single refused dispatch cannot write four pointers for a head that carries a separate code review and a separate figure review, since the sibling dispatchers can each have run; the run directories cited (`classification.json` and `node.json` only, a brief and a claim but no pid) are the composed state either path leaves. The evidence shows a coordinator read `lane-paused`; it does not separate the refused dispatch's own writes from the concurrent duplicates, so the stated root cause is not the one the cited evidence establishes.

findings.reason: the node must distinguish a shut gate from a held/queued answer before changing anything.
findings.text: The endpoint says a `lane-paused` refusal "leaves no pointer, no run directory and no claim for that review", but the base code splits that answer in two: a shut gate queues nothing, while a router hold (`LaneHeld`, a subclass of `LanePaused` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:1321`) deliberately writes a queued pointer so the reviewed run's owed review is not lost (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:4725-4761`, "A router hold on the local lane queues the request: the queued pointer launches later"). The cited incident reports `headroom -5`, which is the router-hold case, and the held pointer is correct state the plan must not remove. Applied literally "for `lane-paused` or any other reason", the repair deletes the queued review the run is owed and turns a queue into no review at all.
